page: Amazon Web Services g7e.4xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, designed for graphics-intensive applications and high-throughput AI workloads. The system is equipped with 16 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor with 8 physical cores operating at 2.4 GHz. System memory comprises 128.0 GB of DDR5 RAM, backed by 320 MB of L3 cache. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPU with 96 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is bundled as a 1900 GB NVMe SSD, accompanied by a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks highlight exceptional capability in specialized tasks, with the instance achieving top-tier scores in LLM inference for prompt processing and text generation across 135M, 7B, and 70B parameter models. Single-core processing performance is strong, as evidenced by a Geekbench score of 2336.0 and single-threaded gzip compression rates of 35.02 GB/sec. Standard multi-core CPU performance and uncached memory bandwidth fall into the average range relative to peer systems, indicating a design focused on GPU-driven compute efficiency rather than pure CPU parallelization.

From a hardware utilization perspective, pairing a 96 GB GPU frame buffer with dedicated local NVMe storage and high-speed memory offers strong cost efficiency for local inference and complex rendering jobs without needing multi-GPU node deployments. Recommended workload fits include large language model inference, graphics rendering, 3D visualization pipelines, and data-intensive AI processing.
